title: A committed workload corpus, and the measurement extended to every channel
description: Sprint 1 measured the plan channels. Real generator and evaluator payloads flow through messages, evaluations and refs, and those are unbounded strings today. Extend the measurement to every channel, and commit a corpus of real payloads that the caps will be derived from and pinned against for ever after -- so that a fixture can never again be the only evidence.

successCriteria.description: A committed workload corpus holds real PlanSpec and SprintContract payloads drawn from .bober/specs/ and .bober/contracts/, plus representative generator and evaluator payloads, each labelled with the channel it exercises.
A function computes, from the corpus, the maximum serialised byte size per channel using the SAME byteSize function the commit boundary uses -- not a reimplementation.
The measurement from sprint 1 is extended to messages, evaluations and refs under corpus-sized payloads, and the results are committed.
A test asserts the corpus is non-empty for every channel the artifact declares, so a channel cannot silently escape measurement by having no corpus entry.
The corpus is committed under version control and its location is documented; a test asserts it is read from disk at test time rather than inlined into the test file.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Changing any cap -- sprint 3 does that, using this corpus.
Trimming the corpus to make a number look better.
stopConditions: A channel has no plausible real payload to measure -- record that fact explicitly rather than inventing one.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: Import byteSize's behaviour rather than reimplementing it: the boundary uses Buffer.byteLength(canonicalJson(value), 'utf8') (src/pge/runtime/commit.ts:257-259). If byteSize is not exported, export it or expose an equivalent through a named helper -- do not hand-roll JSON.stringify, which will disagree with canonical form. GeneratorResult.notes is an unbounded z.string() and real ones run 1,100-1,900 chars, so evaluations is the channel to look at after spec. Draw corpus entries from files already in the repository so the corpus is real rather than synthetic, and record where each entry came from.
evaluatorNotes: Check that the corpus is genuinely real: spot-check that entries correspond to actual files in .bober/specs/ and .bober/contracts/. Check the byte measurement matches the boundary's -- construct a value, run it through both the corpus helper and the real commit boundary, and confirm they agree; a divergence here silently mis-sizes every cap in sprint 3. Verify sc-2-4 bites by deleting a channel's corpus entry and confirming the test fails.
